activities.description: Makes an analogy to doors and bolts in a building to explain cell-to-cell connections
Explains how cell walls separate plant cells and plasmodesmata act as junctions
Discusses how plasmodesmata allow cells to form strong connections and communicate
Explains that plasmodesmata are formed by incomplete cytokinesis
Defines cytokinesis as the division of cytoplasm
Highlights the importance of plasmodesmata for plant viability
Describes the structure of plasmodesmata, including the plasma membrane and the desmotubule
Lists the molecules that can move between plant cells through plasmodesmata
Mentions that some plant viruses spread through plasmodesmata

In some cases, you would want to hold the two adjacent walls formally together and you
might put in some strong bolts or locks.
You might need to ensure that the walls were sealed very tightly together to prevent water
from dripping between them.
In plants, cell walls separate every cell from others.
Cell to cell junctions occur only at holes or gaps in the walls where the plasma membrane
of one cell is continuous with the plasma membrane of neighboring cell.
So the cells in close contact with one another typically through these intercellular junctions
and these intercellular junctions are called Plasma Desmata.

and establish rapid communication between adjacent cells.
